conviction_note: The release falls on a FY guide that Canon revises at every print. Q3 FX beat the plan by about 5.5bn yen of operating profit, while the plan's own Middle East assumption (normal from October) has broken, with Brent at about 90 when the plan was set and 104-117 since. Smaller negatives: the camera industry slowed and Q4 memory cost is rising. The stock has run 13 points ahead of the Nikkei, sits above the consensus target, and has sold 4 of its last 5 prints. Findings sum to -1.3, a mild negative. p_up is 45 on a 5.0% scale, giving -0.5. The scaled number is smaller than the sum because the negatives rest on public series (oil, CIPA, DRAM) that the price can already see, and because a held forecast against a street that already sits below plan would be a relief.
bar: IFIS consensus for FY2026/12 as of 2026-10-26: operating profit 462.4bn yen, pretax 488.4bn, against the company's 465.0bn / 492.0bn raised on 2026-07-27. Source: https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=7751. The company plan is from https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7751&b=k202607270015. print_vs_bar is my expected FY OP after this print (a hold, or a trim to about 460bn) against 462.4bn. The bar is sourced and is a single-vendor consensus. No Q3-only consensus could be sourced: kabuyoho's quarterly line is stale, pre-Q2.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register in the baseline (as of 2026-10-26, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html): 0.78% from one seller, down from 0.86%, so a small short that is covering. 信用倍率 2.71: margin long moderately heavier than margin short. There is no option skew in Japan. Run-up: +7.9% over 20 sessions against the Nikkei's -5.6% over the same window (Yahoo 7751.T and ^N225 daily). Spot 4,937 sits above the IFIS mean target of 4,745 (10 analysts, 7 neutral, 3 bullish) and above kabuyoho's PER/PBR upper bounds (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportTarget?bcode=7751). The short is not crowded, so there is no squeeze fuel. The positioning is a crowded relative-strength long into the print.

findings.finding: Q3 FX beat the plan. USD/JPY averaged 159.25 and EUR/JPY 183.21 in Jul-Sep against the plan's H2 rates of 155/180. Canon's own H2 sensitivity is 1.5bn yen of OP per yen per currency, roughly 0.75bn per quarter, so Q3 gains about 5.5bn yen of OP over plan. Q4 at today's rates (157.7 / 176.2) is roughly -0.8bn, because the euro is below plan. The net FY tailwind is about 4.5-5bn yen, about 1% of OP.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July the FY OP was raised by 9bn yen, with FX contributing +34.1bn, and the stock fell 5.73% the next day (Nikkei -3.95% that day). A FX-led raise has been read as low quality: Fisco wrote on 2026-07-28 that the weaker yen was already being priced (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7751&b=n202607280546).
findings.source: https://global.canon/ja/ir/conference/pdf/conf2026q2j-note.pdf (plan rates and sensitivity, p.6-7); FX averages from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/JPY%3DX?range=6mo&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EURJPY%3DX?range=6mo&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: FX is public and analysts model it, so most of this is priced. What is not priced is how much of it Canon will book into the guide. IFIS consensus OP sits 2.6bn below the company plan, not above it, so the street has not credited the Q3 FX gain to the FY. If it had, consensus would sit at or above 465bn.
findings.independence: None from a separate company-level source. The sensitivity is Canon's own, and the rates are market data.

findings.finding: The plan's Middle East assumption has broken. The July plan priced a 34.6bn yen Middle East hit on the explicit assumption that the situation runs to end-September and sales normalise from October. Brent was about 88-90 when the plan was set; since September it has been 104-117. JRI reported Hormuz transits under 10 ships a day since mid-July. Canon will likely have to push normalisation out again and add oil-linked material and logistics cost in Q4. That offsets the FX gain and makes a held or trimmed FY guide more likely than a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April 2026 the Middle East and memory together drove a FY OP cut from 479bn to 456bn, and the stock fell 7.90% the next day. In October 2025 a 2% OP trim (tariffs) was followed by a 5.46% fall.
findings.source: https://global.canon/ja/ir/conference/pdf/conf2026q2j-note.pdf (p.6, 8: 中東情勢影響 ▲346億円, 売上の正常化は10月以降まで延伸, 9月末までは現在の状態が継続する前提)
findings.why_not_priced: Oil is public. But Canon rose 7.9% over 20 sessions while the Nikkei fell 5.6% and Brent rose from about 104 to 110-117. If the market had marked Canon's Q4 Middle East assumption down, the stock would not have outperformed through the oil spike and would not sit above the consensus target. IFIS consensus is only 0.6% below plan, which is too little to cover a delayed normalisation.
findings.independence: Oil series: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BZ%3DF?range=9mo&interval=1wk. Hormuz status: https://www.oanda.jp/lab-education/market_news/2026_09_04_wtioil/ (2026-09-04, blockade concerns lifting crude). Both are separate from Canon's document.

findings.finding: Camera industry shipments slowed in Q3 against H1. CIPA shows interchangeable-lens shipment value at -15.4% YoY in July and +4.8% in August, roughly -6.6% for Jul-Aug, in yen, so worse in local currency. Total digital camera value fell from about +6% in H1 to about -3% in Jul-Aug. Compacts held at roughly +11%. Canon's plan needs imaging H2 sales up about 11.5% YoY (12,015 FY less 5,527 H1, against H2 2025's 5,821).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on this line. Imaging has been Canon's beat line all year: Q2 imaging OP +78.7% YoY.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: CIPA is public and camera analysts read it, so this is sized small (rule 1). What is left: network cameras and compacts are the growth drivers, and the plan already has imaging H2 OP below H2 2025 (1,915 - 976 = 939bn against 1,026bn). Net of the rest of imaging the miss risk is modest.
findings.independence: None. This is an industry proxy, not Canon's own number.

findings.finding: Q4 memory cost is above the July plan. TrendForce put Q3 conventional DRAM contract prices at +13-18% QoQ. Its September report says contract prices were flat, but vendors are pushing increases to close the gap with server pricing and forward increases were revised sharply up. Canon added only 6bn yen of memory cost in July and said normalisation would take time.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In April 2026 memory cost was the headline of a FY cut and the stock fell 7.90%. In July, memory concern was cited by Fisco as part of the -5.73% day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public series and largely priced, hence the small size. The residual is whether Canon raises the memory hit at this print rather than in January.
findings.independence: https://eetimes.itmedia.co.jp/ee/articles/2607/07/news074.html (2026-07-07, Q3 DRAM +13-18% forecast). Canon's own July note: https://global.canon/ja/ir/conference/pdf/conf2026q2j-note.pdf p.8.

findings.finding: A new buyback with this release is unlikely. Canon finished the 200bn yen, 6.1% buyback on 2026-09-04, five months early (45.33m shares). Its own cash-flow plan ends 2026 at 425bn yen of cash, 1.0 months of turnover and the lowest in its table, with FCF of 290bn against 445bn of financing outflow. Canon's past buybacks were announced at the January FY print and once at a July print, never at an October print in 2024 or 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: January 2026: the FY guide plus the 200bn buyback rose 2.92% the next day. July 2025: a 32m-share buyback announced on 2025-07-29 was followed by three straight up days (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7751&b=n202507300365).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly a non-event. It is filed because the strongest positive this release could carry is a re-upped buyback, and the company's own cash plan argues against one. A holder who bought the run-up hoping for one is left without it.
findings.independence: Canon's cash-flow plan, a different document: https://global.canon/ja/ir/conference/pdf/conf2026q2j-note.pdf p.12.

findings.finding: Counterparty: Canon Marketing Japan, Canon's domestic sales subsidiary, reported on 2026-10-26, after Canon's last print. Jul-Sep pretax rose 26.2% YoY to 14.4bn yen, operating margin went from 6.9% to 8.6%, and 9M progress reached 74.5% against a 70.0% five-year average. It held the FY plan, and its stock was -5.2% this morning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Its own read: a beat with a held plan was sold 5.2% intraday on 2026-10-27, a same-family example of the 'beat but no raise' reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Japan is a small share of Canon's sales, and the domestic strength is IT solutions as much as Canon hardware, so the fundamental read-through is small. It is public since yesterday.

findings.finding: Reaction setup: the stock comes into the print up 7.9% over 20 sessions against the Nikkei's -5.6%, above the IFIS mean target (4,745 yen, 7 of 10 analysts neutral), and with a record of selling its prints. Next-day moves were -4.87% (Jul 2025 trim), -5.46% (Oct 2025 trim), +2.92% (Jan 2026 guide plus buyback), -7.90% (Apr 2026 cut) and -5.73% (Jul 2026 raise).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Computed from Yahoo daily closes on the release dates confirmed by kabutan's 15:30 flashes (2025-07-24, 2025-10-27, 2026-01-29, 2026-04-23, 2026-07-27). The only up reaction carried a buyback.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up component is in the baseline lean (-0.38), which nets to +0.03 after the short-covering terms, so this is partly in the bar already and is sized small. What the lean does not see is the 13-point outperformance against the index and the price sitting above every analyst valuation anchor, which sets a bar a held guide may not clear.

outside_window.finding: Memory-cost normalisation and the KrF lithography doubling are FY2027 guide items for the January print. The Middle East duration is likewise a 2027 question unless it is booked now.

searched_and_found_nothing: kabutan Canon news and TDnet disclosure list for October 2026: no 業績予想の修正 or 配当予想の修正 pre-filed, and no Nikkei 観測 headline before the 10:06 JST seal (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7751, https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7751&nmode=3)

the reason for the October outperformance: no target-price raise or company news found, which reads as rotation out of AI names (kabutan 2026-10-23 '来週の株式相場に向けて＝ＡＩ株急落に歯止めはかかるか')
CIPA September data: not yet published (the August data came out 2026-10-01)
Middle East status for October 2026 from a dated news article: only September reports were found, so the Brent series is used
peer prints from Ricoh, Konica Minolta, Nikon and Epson: none reported yet for Jul-Sep
release_time_source: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=7751&b=k202607270015 (last quarter's 決算短信 '7月27日大引け後(15:30)'; also 15:30 on 2025-10-27 and 2026-04-23). The date 2026-10-27 is confirmed on https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=7751 and kabutan's 決算発表予定日. The release is after the close, so the window runs from the close on 10-27 to the close on 10-28.
bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: very likely, since Canon revised at each of its last four quarterly prints. The likely direction is a hold or small trim, as the Q3 FX gain (about +5bn yen) is offset by a delayed Middle East normalisation and memory cost, against an IFIS bar already 0.6% below plan. Returns: a new buyback is unlikely, given the early completion of the 200bn and a plan ending at 1.0 months of cash; the dividend of 160 yen is likely unchanged. New-year guide: none at a Q3 print. Quarter against its own 進捗率: last year 9M OP was 66.4% of the FY actual (302.4bn / 455.4bn). A Q3 OP of about 100bn yen would put 9M at about 71% of the 465bn plan, which reads well but is inflated by the 58bn tariff refund booked in Q2.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Space theme: Canon is listed among space stocks via Canon Electronics' stake in Space One
rejected_candidates.detail: A theme article with no catalyst in the window. It may partly explain the run-up, and it carries no earnings content.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is flat (+0.03) and the run-up is strongly positive, especially against the index; my findings lean mildly negative and so cut against the run-up. The strongest positive the release could carry is a held or slightly raised FY OP (465bn or more) against an IFIS bar of 462.4bn, helped by a 9M progress rate near 71% and the Q3 FX gain. I looked for a buyback and the company's cash plan argues against one. That relief case is why p_up is 45 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a public series, p_up toward 50): the CIPA finding went from -0.5 to -0.3 and the DRAM finding from -0.3 to -0.2, because both series are public before the print. The Middle East finding went from -1.0 to -0.8 rather than further, because the release is likely to ADD a guide change on it.
Open question 4 (a run-in as a short signal went wrong once): the positioning/run-up finding went from -0.8 to -0.4.

Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): the strongest positive (a held guide against a below-plan street) is written into baseline_tension, and p_up moved from 42 to 45, so expected_move went from -0.8 to -0.5.
The FX (+0.4), buyback (-0.2) and Canon MJ (+0.2) findings were left unchanged.
